title: Building a Safe Pipeline
story: Data flows through your system like water through pipes. Raw text enters one end, and at each junction it's checked, cleaned, and transformed. A single crack — bad input — should stop the flow, not flood the basement.
why: A well-designed pipeline with Result and `?` prevents invalid data from propagating — each checkpoint rejects bad input immediately, keeping downstream code safe.
analogy: A safe pipeline is like airport security — your bag (data) goes through the scanner (parse), gets flagged if it has liquids (validate), and gets the boarding tag only if everything checks out (transform). One red flag and it stays behind.
expected_output:
A
C
Score cannot be negative
Score cannot exceed 100
invalid character in integer string
try_it: Add a fourth stage: `add_bonus(grade: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]`. If the grade is A or B, append a '+' sign. If it's F, return Err("No bonus for failing grade"). Chain it into process_score.
tips: Name pipeline stages clearly: parse_*, validate_*, transform_* — the prefix tells you the purpose
Each stage function takes and returns the same wrapped type — it's Result all the way down
The final `return Ok(...)` marks the end of a successful pipeline run
common_mistakes: Mixing stages — putting validation logic inside parse or transform logic inside validate
Returning pure values from pipeline stages instead of Result — then `?` can't connect them
Forgetting that pipeline stages execute in ORDER — validate runs AFTER parse, so parse errors prevent validation
